message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with your local council in Atlanta. Here’s how it typically works:

1. **Locate the right department**  
   • Noise issues are usually handled by the City of Atlanta’s Code Enforcement Division or the Police Department’s Traffic & Public Safety Unit.  
   • Check the official City of Atlanta website for the most current phone number and email address.  

2. **Gather details**  
   • Date(s) and time(s) of the disturbance.  
   • Location (street address or intersection).  
   • Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs).  
   • Any evidence you have (photos, videos, audio recordings, or witness statements).

3. **Submit the complaint**  
   • Many cities now offer an online portal or mobile app for reporting violations.  
   • If there isn’t an online option, you can call the non‑emergency line (often 311 in many U.S. cities; confirm the exact number for Atlanta).  
   • Provide the information you gathered and ask for a reference number so you can follow up.

4. **Follow up**  
   • Keep the reference number handy.  
   • If you don’t hear back within a reasonable timeframe (usually a few business days), call again using the same reference number.

5. **Know the limits**  
   • City officials will investigate if the noise violates local ordinances (e.g., “noisy vehicles” or “public nuisance”).  
   • They’ll issue citations or fines if the complaint is upheld.  
   • For immediate emergencies (like ongoing violent activity), dial 911 instead.

If you’re unsure which office handles noise complaints in your specific neighborhood, you can also visit the nearest city hall or community center—they often have forms on hand or can direct you to the correct contact point.
